notes: The URL in the brief returns 404. The live JAX Genome Technologies page (/research-and-faculty/resources/scientific-research-services/genome-technologies) publishes no prices. It has no rate card, PDF or iLab link, and it names only 'multiple Illumina short-read instruments' without saying NovaSeq X. The JAX APML page sends pricing questions to an inquiry form. I did not try archive.ph snapshots. The searches turned up no JAX-hosted rate sheet. As a by-product I found a new peer-core datapoint, the University of Illinois Carver Biotechnology Center DNA Services Core. Its price list is effective 1 Aug 2026 and was not on the known list. It shows 8+ lane volume tiers, and its own overhead is added on top of list for external users.
how_to_mine: JAX rates are probably only in iLab or a quote, so JAX is not worth more time. Better targets: (1) the Illinois page https://biotech.illinois.edu/dna-services-core/dna-services-pricing/, and the same core's earlier versions (Wayback) to build a 2024-2026 25B price path. (2) The UConn CGI service-rates page, https://draft.genome.center.uconn.edu/cgi_service_rates, which has Jan 2025 and later versions. (3) The MD Anderson ATGC page (25B $2,595), KUMC, and Dana-Farber internal vs external rates. For each, get Wayback snapshots at 6-month intervals to measure the per-lane price trend.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: A US core's Aug 2026 rate card shows 8+ lane volume discounts that cut the 10B and 25B per-lane price by 6-16%, so tiered discounts are widespread at the core level.
items.detail: University of Illinois DNA Services Core, effective 1 Aug 2026 (internal rates, before overhead): 10B 2x150 lane $2,000 vs $1,710 at 8+ lanes (-14.5%). 10B SR100 lane $1,520 vs $1,270 (-16.4%). 25B 2x150 lane $3,380 vs $3,180 (-5.9%). 25B SR100 lane $2,190 vs $1,930 (-11.9%). The 25B 2x150 list is about $2.26/Gb on the 1.5B-style roughly 1,500 Gb spec, which was not verified, so it is not a firm $/Gb. External users pay an extra 30.8% overhead (20% cap for Illinois state institutions). The page says 'custom quotes are often lower than list'. A full-wafer price of $3,310 against $3,380 for one 25B lane is also notable, but that line is ambiguous.
items.source_name: University of Illinois Carver Biotechnology Center DNA Services Core
items.quote: custom quotes are often lower than list price
items.why_new: The Illinois core is not among the cores already covered; the volume-tier structure is a new observation. The tier percentages come from list prices (my calculation).

items.label: 2A
items.claim: Academic cores layer discounts: tiers for 8+ lanes, internal rates below external, and quotes below list. Research buyers therefore sit at the low end of Illumina's effective price.
items.detail: The University of Illinois core lists NovaSeq X Plus lanes at $1,160 for a 10B split lane, $1,710 for 10B at 8+ lanes, and $3,180 for 25B at 8+ lanes. It also lists PacBio Revio at $2,200 per SMRT cell ($2,120 at 4+ cells) and ONT GridION flowcells at $1,470. A large bulk buyer therefore gets about 6-16% off, and the core's rates exclude off-campus overhead (+30.8% external). Cross-platform pricing was also on the page, so a researcher can price an Illumina lane against long-read alternatives in the same core.
items.source_name: University of Illinois Carver Biotechnology Center DNA Services Core
items.why_new: Adds a new core with tiered pricing and non-Illumina platform pricing; it is an Illinois-specific observation and it is a list price, not a trend.
